210-author-body-cues-llm.did: Authored 68 body cues across 113.7s to 2040.2s. Built the video around three per-tool series that each cover all five tools: a glass tile for each tool in the spoken overview, a tool-intro section opener at each tool's demo boundary, and a single five-row comparison table at the head-to-head verdict. The three-node chain from the concept is enacted once as a real pipeline card when the demo scenario is described, then tracked through every tool's build with Trigger, AI and Send lower-thirds, so the same chain is visibly re-skinned five times. Only 15 of the 68 cues are fullframe because the body is 1697s of screen recording; the demo stretches are carried by overlays that add the narration's point rather than echoing the click.
210-author-body-cues-llm.issues: Seven lint warnings, no errors, and all seven are deliberate. Two W6 bare stretches sit in the Flowise and Make pricing pages, where the rulebook forbids per-tool pricing graphics because the pricing page is already on screen, so I left them bare rather than decorate them. One W7 bare stretch and both W21 long-holds come from two beat cards that stay on screen while they build, the chain card at 249s and the 5-row verdict table at 1412s, so the screen is never actually empty there even though the lint measures cue starts. The two W14 zone-underserved warnings are just the intro and conclusion having no cues yet, which the zone pass fills next. Three things I deliberately did NOT do: no card restates the on-screen scorecard values, no Zapier card sits at the 286s recording error where the narration names the wrong tool, and no card carries the three ASR garbles at 978s, 1208s or 1673s. I also used no stat-hit cues at all, because every big number in this video is a pricing figure that is already on the page being shown.

130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.did: Wrote the 17-beat screenplay enacting the approved toll-gate direction across the whole 113.7s intro: the chain assembles behind the presenter, a gate rises in its path, and the gate then charges three different currencies in turn — hours (a clock dragged out, config panels bolted on), capability (two of three blocks shaved off so it fits, then it hits a wall), and finally nothing at all, which is the film's turn to the light register. The middle stretch queues five identically-built chains at the same gate, resets them to identical for the fair-test section, and strips the gate's logo plates on 'no marketing claims'; the tease runs all five crossings at speed and sorts the residue into four counted columns; the button retracts the gate and leaves two intact chains standing where it was.
130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.issues: Beat times are derived from word timings rather than estimated — each beat is anchored to a verbatim clause and boundaries sit at the midpoint of the pause between clauses. First build failed lint with ten E2 errors because my clauses were shorter than the sentences containing them, so each beat trailed its own clause into the following pause; fixed by extending eight clauses to fill their beats rather than by moving the beat boundaries. Intents deliberately repeat (2-4 beats per intent, still in default-arc order) because a one-beat-per-intent screenplay would put every beat far past the 12s ceiling on a 113.7s intro — deviation_reason records this on every beat.
130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.output: intro-film/screenplay.json — 17 beats covering 0 to 113.667s contiguously, lint-screenplay clean with zero errors and zero warnings; longest beat 11.2s, register flips five times, presenter full-frame on b01 and b17
